My hobbies include poorly maintaining too many bicycles, running distances that are too far, GM-ing TTRPGs, and, well, more software development obviously.","visibility":"public","followers_count":20,"following_count":0,"starred_repos_count":4,"username":"mfenniak"},"title":"fix: resolve access to Forgejo's internal unix socket the same for Forgejo server and SSH sessions","body":"Fixes #14755. Changes the default `[server].INTERNAL_LISTENER_PATH` to `run/forgejo.sock` (note: relative, not an absolute `/run`), instead of being defined by `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` with a fallback to an absolute `/run/forgejo/internal.sock`. A relative path here is interpreted as relative to the app.ini `WORK_PATH`. As the app.ini file is passed to both Forgejo and ssh connections to Forgejo, the same calculated path is used regardless of any differences in environment variables provided to the different processes. This allows the same default value to be used for server installations and local development with reasonable behaviour. If the default config value is used, the socket will be created in a `run` folder, right next to `custom` and `data`. The `run` directory allows Forgejo to set-up appropriate permissions on the directory `run` before creating the socket, to prevent a race condition case where the socket is world-accessible before it is chmod'd with correct permissions. (Otherwise, `forgejo.sock` would've been a reasonable new default.) Manually tested that this configuration works in an OpenSSH server, with an systemd-run Forgejo, by setting `[server].INTERNAL_LISTENER_PATH` to the new default value. ### Compliance - [x] I confirm that I make this contribution in accordance with [Forgejo's AI Agreement](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/governance/src/commit/9084720dc6a7fbf1d3f358919d46bd6adfb55287/AIAgreement.md). ### Tests for Go changes - I added test coverage for Go changes... - [ ] in their respective `*_test.go` for unit tests. - [ ] in the `tests/integration` directory if it involves interactions with a live Forgejo server. - I ran... - [x] `make pr-go` before pushing ### Documentation - [ ] I created a pull request [to the documentation](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/docs) to explain to Forgejo users how to use this change. - If this approach moves forward, I'll make a documentation PR with the same update. - [ ] I did not document these changes and I do not expect someone else to do it. ### Release notes - [ ] This change will be noticed by a Forgejo user or admin (feature, bug fix, performance, etc.). I suggest to include a release note for this change. - [x] This change is not visible to a Forgejo user or admin (refactor, dependency upgrade, etc.). The `INTERNAL_TOKEN` can now be dropped from the configuration, and the UNIX socket path can be configured using the `INTERNAL_LISTENER_PATH` options. This change removes the `./forgejo generate secret INTERNAL_TOKEN` command and updates the contrib Forgejo systemd unit file. The `forgejo.service` example systemd file has been updated to set `RuntimeDirectory=forgejo`, which is a recommended setting for all systemd users.

Fork pull requests against a repository with Forgejo Action workflows that use the `on.pull_request_review` and `on.pull_request_review_comment` event were not correctly identified as forked pull requests. Forgejo Actions treats forked pull requests in special manners, including requiring approval before their workflows are executed, and omiting secrets from their execution context. These protections were disabled on these workflows, which could be triggered on the forked pull request after creation. The vulnerability has been addressed by correcting the identification of these events, and covering all forked pull request event executions with extensive related integration tests to ensure no other events were subject to this error. - fix: avoid loading unnecessary data during tag creation [patch PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14785). When creating a tag via the release API, the implementation for loading related objects was invoked on an unsaved release object with a `0` ID. This caused unrelated release attachment metadata to be loaded into memory, and in the case of tag creation via the API, returned as part of the API response. The related loading routines have been disabled when the object is unsaved. (This patch was not included in the embargoed security patches from the 2026-10-12 security release, as its security implications were not known at the time it was authored. It is documented here for awareness of the security risk being addressed in this release.) - fix: prevent reading arbitrary label metadata. The API `DELETE /repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/{index}/labels/{identifier}` allows identifiers to be either a label name, or a label unique database identifier (`.id` field in API responses). The API performs write access checks against the repository, and the unique database identifier can be a label from a different repository. The resulting delete operation is a no-op as an issue on one repository cannot contain a label from another repository, but the label metadata may be leaked by the API response. To fix the issue, labels are queried by the repository of the API invocation. - fix: prevent deletion of labels from org/repo with mismatched ownership. The APIs `DELETE /orgs/{org}/labels/{id}` and `DELETE /repos/{owner}/{repo}/labels/{id}` accessed a common internal function to delete a label within their parent organization or repository. As this common codepath didn't differentiate the owner identity, a common database identifier being used by an organization and a repository could be confused as to the true owner of a label, confounding the permission checks on the owner. The issue has been fixed by separating and distinguising the codepaths. ## Release notes - Security bug fixes - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14811): 2026-10-12 security patches ","labels":[{"id":201023,"name":"bug/confirmed","exclusive":true,"is_archived":false,"color":"e11d21","description":"it can be reproduced","url":"https://codeberg.org/api/v1/repos/forgejo/forgejo/labels/201023"},{"id":79184,"name":"forgejo/security","exclusive":false,"is_archived":false,"color":"eb6420","description":"Security (please disclose responsibly)","url":"https://codeberg.org/api/v1/repos/forgejo/forgejo/labels/79184"},{"id":201030,"name":"test/present","exclusive":true,"is_archived":false,"color":"5319e7","description":"test has been added","url":"https://codeberg.org/api/v1/repos/forgejo/forgejo/labels/201030"},{"id":209916,"name":"worth a release-note","exclusive":false,"is_archived":false,"color":"f6c6c7","description":"Add this PR to the release notes","url":"https://codeberg.org/api/v1/repos/forgejo/forgejo/labels/209916"}],"milestone":{"id":145608,"title":"Forgejo v18.0.0","description":" ## Release notes - Security bug fixes - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14811): 2026-10-12 security patches - Breaking security features - [PR](https://codeberg.org/forgejo/forgejo/pulls/14148): Move internal communication to UNIX socket. The `INTERNAL_TOKEN` can now be dropped from the configuration, and the UNIX socket path can be configured using the `INTERNAL_LISTENER_PATH` options.
